requirements_addressed: Keycloak JWT token validation with PyJWT + PyJWKClient
Signature verification via JWKS (cached, kid-rotation aware)
RS256-only algorithm allowlist (blocks alg:none and HS256)
Student claim extraction with fail-closed semantics
Issuer pinning (ts.net name vs tailnet IP)
Comprehensive hermetic test suite (no live Keycloak)
Seam test for OIDC_SETTINGS integration contract

completion_promises.criterion_text: KeycloakTokenResolver in src/study_tutor/http/auth_keycloak.py implements TokenResolver and validates signature, iss, aud, exp/nbf (60s leeway), and an RS256-only algorithm allowlist
completion_promises.evidence: KeycloakTokenResolver implements the TokenResolver protocol with async resolve() method. Uses PyJWT.decode() with algorithms=['RS256'] allowlist, validates issuer via issuer= parameter, audience via audience= parameter, exp/nbf with leeway=60 from settings. Tests verify RS256 validation, alg:none rejection, HS256 rejection, issuer validation, audience validation, expiration, and not-yet-valid handling.

completion_promises.criterion_text: The student_id claim (name from OIDCSettings.student_claim) is extracted only after validation; a missing claim raises Unauthenticated, never a 500
completion_promises.evidence: Claim extraction happens in Step 3 of resolve() method, after all PyJWT validation passes. Missing/empty/non-string student_id claim raises Unauthenticated with descriptive message. Test test_missing_student_claim_raises_unauthenticated verifies this behavior.

completion_promises.criterion_text: Every negative path (bad signature, wrong issuer, wrong audience, expired, not-yet-valid, alg:none/HS256, unknown kid, unreachable JWKS, garbage token) raises Unauthenticated and raises no unexpected error
completion_promises.evidence: All PyJWT exceptions (ExpiredSignatureError, ImmatureSignatureError, InvalidIssuerError, InvalidAudienceError, InvalidAlgorithmError, InvalidSignatureError, DecodeError, InvalidTokenError) are caught and converted to Unauthenticated. PyJWKClientError from JWKS fetch failures also raises Unauthenticated. Final catch-all Exception handler ensures fail-closed behavior. Tests cover all negative paths: bad signature, unknown kid, wrong issuer/audience, expired, not-yet-valid, alg:none, HS256, unreachable JWKS, garbage token.

completion_promises.criterion_text: Issuer used for iss validation stays the ts.net name even when the JWKS fetch URL is overridden to a tailnet IP (KC-D2)
completion_promises.evidence: KeycloakTokenResolver.__init__ stores expected_issuer=settings.issuer (the ts.net name) separately from jwks_url. PyJWT.decode() uses issuer=self.expected_issuer for validation, not derived from JWKS URL. Test test_issuer_validation_uses_ts_net_name verifies that tokens with ts.net issuer pass validation while tokens with IP issuer fail, even when JWKS URL is the IP address.

completion_promises.criterion_text: Hermetic tests mint their own keys and monkeypatch JWKS — no live realm and no network
completion_promises.evidence: Tests use cryptography library to generate RSA keypairs in rsa_keypair fixture. mint_token() helper creates test JWTs signed with test keys. mock_pyjwkclient fixture monkeypatches PyJWKClient.get_signing_key_from_jwt to return test public keys without network calls. All 15 tests pass without requiring external Keycloak realm or network access.
